page: Microsoft Azure D2alds_v7 is a low-memory virtual machine instance belonging to the Daldsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical AMD EPYC 9V45 core with 2 threads, operating at a base clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The instance is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Local storage is bundled, consisting of a 118 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is capable of premium storage integration.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The high clock speed of the AMD EPYC processor enables top-tier single-core performance, as demonstrated by stress-ng single-core CPU tests and single-threaded compression and decompression tasks, both ranking in the top 10%. However, due to the low core count, multi-core CPU performance and Passmark CPU scores fall into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth is average for large uncached blocks but weak for small cached blocks.

The D2alds_v7 offers a cost-efficient entry point for workloads requiring high single-threaded performance and fast local storage without the overhead of large memory footprints. The 118 GB NVMe SSD provides rapid local read and write capabilities, but the 4.0 GB memory limit restricts its suitability for memory-intensive applications. This instance is best suited for lightweight single-threaded tasks, small-scale web serving, development environments, and basic utility workloads that benefit from high CPU clock speeds and local SSD storage but do not require extensive parallel processing.
